lines.text: A spinning motor is also a generator. The faster it spins, the harder it pushes back against the battery.
So its push fades with speed. At low speed our motors could give twenty-six meters per second squared. At four meters per second, about ten. At top speed, zero.
Slow, the tires are the limit. Fast, the motors are. The code checks which one is smaller, using a planning current of one hundred fifty amps.
Braking is different: the motors aren't fighting their own speed, so only grip limits it.
